chapters.markdown:
# Configuration and Seed recovery

The recovery inputs remain separate: a Wizard configuration backup, a completed
Harvest Seed, and freshly fetched System source including its pinned Wizard
submodule. Configuration is not copied into Harvest, and no service-data download
is provided by the Wizard.

The Wizard imports literal shell assignments, including single/double
quotes, escaped metacharacters and equals signs. Backup preserves unmodelled
runtime settings in `main.runtimeOptions` / project `runtimeOptions`, including
image references and host port bindings. JSON and ZIP exports contain secrets;
protect them as you protect the running configuration. Shell expressions requiring
expansion or execution are rejected; provide their literal resolved values instead.
The original Cube header and its strict format validation remain unchanged.

## Choose the working directory and backup target

Live working data and Seed backup storage are independent. Fresh installations
use local working data on the system disk; an external target is required only
while making or reading a backup. Put the host-owned selectors in a mode-0600
file, for example `/etc/system-bootstrapper/persistence.env`:

```sh
PERSISTENCE_MODE=local
PERSISTENT_DIR=/var/lib/system-bootstrapper/platform
SEED_MOUNT=/media/bootstrapper-backup
SEED_DIR=/media/bootstrapper-backup/seed
SEED_UUID=REPLACE_WITH_BACKUP_FILESYSTEM_UUID
```

Mount the actual existing backup filesystem and create its `seed` directory
before an operation. The mount/UUID checks prevent a missing external disk from
being replaced by an accidental local directory. For local live storage, select an external backup filesystem distinct from the
system disk. Legacy volume-backed layouts may retain a disjoint Seed on their
selected retained volume. The target must be disjoint from live data; see the [storage guide](PERSISTENT_VOLUME.md). Normal startup,
configuration changes and TLS renewal do not require this medium. Deleting a VM
with local working data deletes that data, so preserve a completed external Seed
and its matching configuration before depending on a replacement host.

## Creating a completed recovery Seed

Install host integration with `bootstrapper/install-volume-host.sh` so scheduled
Certbot renewals use `system-certbot`. For manual renewal and renewal dry-runs,
use the same wrapper, for example `system-certbot renew --dry-run`. It shares a
filesystem lease with Harvest. Do not run an unmanaged Certbot command or modify
certificate state manually during Harvest.

An explicit Harvest launches a transient helper from the exact controller image;
ordinary controller/GitLab containers keep no `/seed` binding. The helper checks
backup availability, host mount identity, permissions and free space before
quiescing any service. It obtains the global live-data lease at
`configuration/.storage-operation-lock` and the renewal lease, explicitly stops
GitLab's services with a bounded longer runit wait, independently verifies that
every enabled service is down, then stops the container. Inspection, service
quiescence and container shutdown share a 120-second budget. The final container
exit must be zero and Docker must not report an OOM kill.
A forced shutdown is rejected rather than described as a consistent database copy.
While GitLab is stopped, the authenticated Sync status/Fetch API remains available;
configuration and other control mutations are rejected. GitLab/registry writes are
unavailable for the duration of this cold backup.

Harvest copies `/srv`, `/ssl` and the mounted Certbot account/renewal state into a
new private staging directory. Disposable Unix sockets, FIFOs and device nodes
are excluded; services recreate their process endpoints. A manifest records all file checksums, ownership,
permissions, symlink targets and the GitLab version/edition reference and image content ID. The staged
payload is verified before publishing `seed/current`, an atomic link to a completed
`seed/snapshots/<generation>`. Previous snapshots and historical `seed/srv` /
`seed/ssl` trees are retained. They are not automatically pruned; provide room for
the new snapshot. Copy failure leaves the previous completed snapshot selected.
GitLab is resumed on normal completion, failure or handled termination. If a
service stop fails while the container is still running, Harvest requests every
enabled service to run again; starting an already running container would not
resume those services. An uncertain remote stop is allowed to reach its bounded
deadline before resumption, so an old stop cannot race the restart. On failure,
Harvest prints only the container's running state, exit code and OOM flag.

SIGKILL, a lost host or power failure cannot execute cleanup. A remaining
`configuration/.storage-operation-lock`, backup `.operation-lock` or
`.system-bootstrapper-certificate-lock` is deliberate evidence
of an interrupted operation. Verify no Harvest/restore/renewal process remains,
start GitLab if necessary, and remove only the stale lease before retrying. Do not
promote a `.harvest-*` staging directory to `current`.

### Run from the Wizard or the host

With the target available, **Harvest** in the authenticated Wizard uses the
same repository-owned dispatcher as `system/harvest.sh`. You can instead run
from a reviewed host checkout using an available, accepted complete controller
image. Resolve and record its actual image identity, then use:

```sh
sudo env PERSISTENCE_ENV_FILE=/etc/system-bootstrapper/persistence.env \
  bash bootstrapper/seed-operation.sh harvest \
  --image sha256:REPLACE_WITH_ACCEPTED_CONTROLLER_IMAGE_ID \
  --check-only
sudo env PERSISTENCE_ENV_FILE=/etc/system-bootstrapper/persistence.env \
  bash bootstrapper/seed-operation.sh harvest \
  --image sha256:REPLACE_WITH_ACCEPTED_CONTROLLER_IMAGE_ID
```

`--check-only` validates inputs without stopping services or copying payload.
A completed operation removes its owned helper. Only then detach the backup
medium. Save the corresponding **Wizard configuration backup** independently;
Harvest does not add that configuration to the Seed.

## Restore an external Seed into a fresh local installation

The inputs are the completed Seed, matching Wizard `bootstrapper.zip`, recorded
System source with its pinned submodule, and declared image references or
verified image archives. The former live data directory is not an input.

1. Install Docker on the replacement Ubuntu host and check out the intended
   source revision with pinned submodules. Select `PERSISTENCE_MODE=local` and
   a fresh local `PERSISTENT_DIR`, or explicitly select a mounted live volume.
   Mount the retained backup filesystem and set its `SEED_MOUNT`, `SEED_DIR`
   and expected UUID in the private host selector. Do not start GitLab yet.
   Prepare only the live directories and persistence marker from this selector:

   ```sh
   sudo env PERSISTENCE_ENV_FILE=/etc/system-bootstrapper/persistence.env \
     bash -euc 'set -a; source "$PERSISTENCE_ENV_FILE"; source bootstrapper/storage-env.sh; set +a; exec bash bootstrapper/persistence.sh'
   ```

   This step neither starts containers nor requires the backup medium. It must
   precede `--check-only` on a fresh target: that preflight does not create paths.
2. Make the accepted complete controller image and exact harvested GitLab image
   available. Rebuild source-built images from their recorded source and pull
   public images at their recorded references. A custom mutable tag is not a
   recoverable artifact. Preserve immutable private Wizard registry pins: their
   payload must be in the Seed rather than replaced by another build.
3. Keep the configuration ZIP in a private absolute path on the new host. Run
   the repository-owned host restore entry point with the accepted image:

   ```sh
   sudo env PERSISTENCE_ENV_FILE=/etc/system-bootstrapper/persistence.env \
     bash bootstrapper/seed-operation.sh restore \
     --image sha256:REPLACE_WITH_ACCEPTED_CONTROLLER_IMAGE_ID \
     --configuration-backup /root/recovery/bootstrapper.zip \
     --check-only
   sudo env PERSISTENCE_ENV_FILE=/etc/system-bootstrapper/persistence.env \
     bash bootstrapper/seed-operation.sh restore \
     --image sha256:REPLACE_WITH_ACCEPTED_CONTROLLER_IMAGE_ID \
     --configuration-backup /root/recovery/bootstrapper.zip
   ```

   Storage selection belongs to this host; old exported working paths must not
   override it. The helper validates the completed Seed and exact GitLab
   image/version/edition before service-data writes. Fresh empty scaffold
   directories and an explicitly imported configuration are allowed; existing
   live GitLab/TLS data is refused instead of overwritten. A corrupt or
   incomplete Seed does not become a valid restore source.
4. Restore copies only after validation. It durably creates
   `gitlab/data/.system-bootstrapper-restore-incomplete` before copying and
   durably removes it after verifying the restored payload. A failed copy keeps
   this guard; controller/GitLab startup refuses partly restored state. Inspect
   the failed operation and preserve its partial target and marker for diagnosis.
   After confirming its helper has ended, select another fresh live directory
   and restore the same verified Seed there. The native entry point refuses to
   resume over partial data; do not delete its marker or start writers manually.
5. Restore preserves the Seed's ownership and modes exactly. Older snapshots may
   contain an SSL root with mode `0700`, which prevents NGINX workers from serving
   HTTP-01 challenges. Before starting writers or certificate renewal, repeat the
   native preparation command from step 1. It prepares the public challenge
   directory and adds traversal permission to the SSL root while keeping private
   certificate directories and key files unchanged. The retained Seed is unchanged.
   Install Certbot as needed and run
   `sudo bash bootstrapper/install-volume-host.sh`. This rebinds webroot renewal
   paths to the new live directory and installs the renewal/deploy integration.
   Set the required image selectors, then start with `sudo bash start.sh`.
   Reprovision optional Review/Beta helpers explicitly if their old immutable
   image is absent; see the [environment procedure](../project-bootstrap/wizard-environments/README.md).
   Runner managers/workspaces are recreated from configuration and restored
   GitLab state; old runner directories are not required inputs.
6. Verify authenticated Fetch, Wizard/GitLab/registry access, restored data and
   runner CI. After helper completion, unmount/detach the backup medium and
   verify configuration Push/restart and TLS renewal still work. They use only
   the new local live directory. Use `sudo system-certbot renew --dry-run`
   when configured DNS and certificate lineages are reachable.

Startup never applies a Seed automatically. Merely reattaching an old live-data
volume is a separate reuse path, not this backup-to-fresh-local restore.

If a controller restarts with a storage or upgrade lease and no incomplete-restore
marker, it pauses before starting writers and remains available to native recovery through
`docker exec`. It does not resume automatically when the lease disappears.
After completing the applicable recovery and confirming the live target is safe,
restart it deliberately with `sudo docker restart system_bootstrapper_1`.
An incomplete Seed restore still requires a different fresh target as above.

### Pulling a restored private Wizard image

After GitLab starts, `system/ensure-wizard-image.sh` recovers an absent immutable
Wizard image from the platform's own registry. It validates the saved managed
Wizard receipt and registry/project identity, renders a GitLab/registry-only proxy,
and waits for GitLab's internal readiness endpoint. GitLab creates a project deploy
token with only `read_registry`; Docker receives the password on standard input
and writes its login to a new private temporary directory. The helper pulls and
verifies the exact saved digest, revokes the token on success or failure, and
removes the temporary login. Old host Docker credentials are not recovery inputs.
Normal public-image startup and already cached exact pins need no token.

The deploy token has GitLab's next-day UTC expiry as a safety bound and is normally
revoked immediately. See the [GitLab deploy-token documentation](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/deploy_tokens/).
Only tokens with the reserved recovery purpose in the receipt's exact project are
eligible for cleanup. A failed revocation retains
`configuration/.wizard-image-recovery.pending`; startup must finish that cleanup
even if the image has since been cached. An interrupted process leaves
`configuration/.wizard-image-recovery.lock`. After verifying the old process has
ended, remove only that stale lock and retry startup; retain the pending file so
the helper can revoke the reserved credential. Credential failures stop startup
before Wizard and project services rather than substituting a different image.

## Verification boundaries

`tests/seed/recovery-contract.py` exercises the real shell scripts and rsync with a
fixture Docker command, including failed copies, forced shutdown, version mismatch,
corruption, missing completion markers, active writers, renewal locking and
interrupted-copy durability. Wizard model regressions cover literal assignments,
JSON/ENV/ZIP equivalence and the immutable signature.

The required [disposable platform scenario](../tests/e2e/README.md) additionally
runs real GitLab/runner/registry CI, exports configuration through the actual
Wizard model, removes the original private host and restores only declared
fresh-source images, configuration ZIP and completed external Seed into a
different empty local directory. It exercises missing backup storage and global
live-lease exclusion, refuses nonempty restore targets and corrupted payloads,
then detaches backup mounts before the real configuration Push/restart, runner
CI and TLS-renewal checks. It checks restored service/data identities, uncached private Wizard image
recovery and actual ACME account/renewal/deployment through a local authority.
These checks do not emulate a new VM's OS installation or systemd timer scheduling.

The retained-volume `recover-volume.sh` path is separate: its image archives are
explicit inputs, whereas the configuration-plus-Seed scenario rebuilds declared
custom images from source. Neither path makes an older Seed a matching backup for
a newer configuration. Capture compatible inputs and verify the intended GitLab
image identity before recovery.

chapters.title: 8. Evolving a running system
chapters.markdown:
## 5. Evolving a running system

System evolution uses the development platform to change the source from which
its successor is built. Generation **A** hosts the source, requirements, merge
request, runner and image registry. Its pipeline builds and tests generation
**B**. After review and a deliberate promotion, B supplies the same machinery
for the next change. Merely restarting A or rebuilding an unchanged image does
not demonstrate an improvement.

The source is the DNA; service state is a separate input. Neither a public code
mirror nor a container image contains an installation's users, repositories,
issues, merge requests, registry blobs or encryption secrets. A successor must
preserve those inputs as well as reproduce the container definitions.

### 5.1 Prerequisites and ownership

The host promotion commands below target the Ubuntu installation with a
configured GitLab HTTPS origin. The local WSL/HTTP first-install path is separate.
Before opening the change, prepare the following:

| Input | Requirement |
| --- | --- |
| Accepted source | A clean, reviewed System revision and its exact recursive Wizard submodule commit. Every initialization, recovery, verification and deployment entry point must be versioned in that checkout. |
| Existing generation | Record the GitLab version and edition, immutable service-image references and controller/Wizard source identities. Saved configuration takes precedence over first-install examples. |
| Candidate resources | A trusted runner/host with capacity for Production and a separate disposable platform, including image archives and database copies. Obtain the resource lease before starting the heavy job. The current harness allows 12 GiB candidate RAM; this is not the total host requirement. |
| Isolated state | Separate candidate containers, networks, Docker daemon and data directories. Never attach A's writable database or registry directories to B while A is running. |
| Recovery checkpoint | A completed, checksum-verified cold Harvest or an equivalently consistent supported backup, matching configuration, GitLab secrets and the exact previous images. Preserve the full Certbot account/renewal tree and any separately configured external storage. |
| Independent recovery access | SSH/console access, the accepted checkout or Git bundle, required image archives, private storage selectors and credentials remain available while the platform's own GitLab is down. |
| Promotion authority | An authorized maintenance window, a named operator/coordinator, the exact candidate evidence and a recovery decision point. A successful merge alone does not authorize arbitrary Production changes. |

Use your own domains, selected working storage and private credentials. Keep
installation-specific selectors, backups, logs and receipts outside Git. The
repository owns the logic that produces and validates them; it does not contain
an operator's passwords or data. Transfer secrets through the entry point's
private inputs, never through a public pipeline specification or job log.

The [candidate harness](../tests/e2e/README.md) uses a privileged private Docker
daemon and therefore requires trusted code. Its resource limits are ceilings,
not a reservation or a disk quota. A small host capable of serving the Wizard
and GitLab is not necessarily capable of testing a second full platform.

### 5.2 Develop B through A's merge-request workflow

1. Record the intended improvement and acceptance criteria in the installation's
   selected tracker. Create a branch from the accepted default branch.
2. Change the committed image selectors, build recipes, tools and documentation
   together. Pin the exact GitLab edition/version and image digest. Do not use a
   floating tag to select the successor. Retain the previous accepted pins.
3. Open a GitLab merge request. Test the committed revision; uncommitted local
   edits or private wrappers are not part of the candidate. A missing operation
   must be implemented and reviewed here before it is used on a live host.
4. Keep the required merge gates enabled. Documentation-only changes use the
   short documentation lane; image, CI, script and infrastructure changes use
   the complete runtime lane. Do not classify an upgrade as documentation to
   avoid migration testing.
5. Review the implementation and its evidence, merge only when the required
   current pipeline succeeds, and delete the merged working branch. The merged
   default-branch revision receives its own applicable checks before promotion.

The pipeline stages and their evidence are described in the
[test guide](../tests/README.md#full-system-and-platform-gates). Component checks
run without the host socket or network inside their child containers.
`test:candidate-image` builds the complete System image from committed inputs.
`test:platform-candidate` serializes the resource-heavy real platform checks and
must pass before runtime publishing. The pipeline's resource group complements,
but does not replace, host capacity checks and the operator's resource lease.

When public distribution is enabled, the Docker Hub publication job follows
these required checks on the protected default branch or a protected version
tag. It copies the accepted complete controller and matching Wizard rather
than rebuilding either after acceptance. Each receives a full-source-commit
tag; a protected `vX.Y.Z` tag can add a version alias. The release receipt binds
source revision/tree, Wizard gitlink, image IDs and immutable Docker Hub
references. Existing conflicting aliases are rejected, and anonymous pull
verification checks that both public images can be retrieved without publisher
credentials. See [publisher configuration](../Prepare-Host.md#publish-your-own-public-releases).

Public publication does not promote Production or back up service data. A new
operator selects that accepted source plus the two digest references and uses
`bootstrapper/install-release.py` through the fresh-install handbook path.
Existing installations retain their saved selectors and require the appropriate
reviewed promotion/migration procedure instead.

For the declared GitLab migration, the disposable candidate has one shared
40-minute execution budget; the CI job has a 45-minute deadline including image
preparation, publication and cleanup. These are upper bounds, not a prediction
that every change takes that long. Documentation-only changes retain their short
lane. No earlier passing fixture or MR run replaces the required acceptance for
the exact merged source being promoted.

### 5.3 Validate existing-state migration, not only first startup

A blank B starting successfully does not prove that A can be upgraded. Validate
the transition using representative state created at A's GitLab version, then
move only a consistent copy into the isolated candidate:

1. Establish representative users, repositories, issues, merge requests and
   discussions, encrypted settings and a registry image. Record identities and
   repository/image hashes as private test oracles.
2. Stop all writers through the supported backup procedure and verify the
   checkpoint before copying. Keep the original generation or its recoverable
   checkpoint separate from the candidate's writable data.
3. Start the candidate with the proposed GitLab image and allow required regular
   and background migrations to complete. Check GitLab's readiness and migration
   state; a running Docker container alone is insufficient.
4. Verify preserved identities, encrypted settings and registry pulls, then run
   a real runner build/push/pull pipeline. Exercise a deliberately failing job
   to prove that downstream delivery is blocked. Verify authenticated Sync
   Fetch, the exact System Cube, Wizard routing and persistent mount boundaries.
5. Exercise failure and recovery. Remove only exactly owned candidate resources;
   retain sanitized source/image/stage evidence and cleanup receipts. Candidate
   data archives and secrets must not become public CI artifacts.

The existing configuration-plus-Seed scenario provides representative state and
cold-recovery checks; see its
[verification boundary](RECOVERY_CONTRACT.md#verification-boundaries). A check
that restores to the same GitLab version is not, by itself, evidence of a
cross-version migration. Require explicit source-version and target-version
migration results for an upgrade.

### 5.4 Example: a GitLab security patch is a system evolution

The committed [security release profile](../gitlab/security-release.json)
declares a GitLab CE **19.4.3 → 19.5.3** transition and a GitLab Runner
**19.4.0 → 19.5.1** transition with its matching helper. The linked upstream
[patch advisory](https://docs.gitlab.com/releases/patches/patch-release-gitlab-19-5-3-released/)
and [Docker upgrade guidance](https://docs.gitlab.com/update/docker/) describe
its prerequisites. Required database and post-deployment migrations must finish;
check the source/target upgrade path rather than treating any newer image as an
interchangeable patch.

The selected System/CI images and new versioned Wizard recipes also install the
committed public CA bundle. Existing reserved recipe hashes remain valid and do
not silently acquire a different trust store: upgrade such recipes explicitly.
These inputs and their tests are part of the reviewed candidate, alongside the
service versions. Runtime configuration still supplies any installation-specific
private certificate authorities separately.

Here the improvement is measurable: the accepted target image contains the
specified upstream fixes, the previous database migrates successfully, and
projects, credentials and the platform's build/delivery behavior remain usable.
A hosts the merge request and runs these tests for B; changing the image directly
on the live host first would bypass that evolution process.

A single-node GitLab has downtime during this patch's database migration. The
Wizard's two-container proxy switch does not turn a GitLab database upgrade into
a zero-downtime rollout. Do not run old and new GitLab versions against the same
live data or promise that switching NGINX back reverses a database migration.

### 5.5 Promote the accepted successor

Before stopping A, retain the accepted source and required tools outside the
GitLab service being upgraded. Preserve the exact image evidence and a verified
checkpoint on storage that remains accessible during maintenance. Preload the
required images if their registry will be unavailable during the switch. A
prepublished accepted mirror or Git bundle, including the required pinned
submodule sources, breaks the dependency on needing GitLab to recover GitLab; a
private local script does not.

To retain source independently, run these standard Git commands from the clean
accepted checkout on your management host while its sources are available:

```bash
umask 077
git submodule update --init --recursive
SOURCE_BUNDLE_DIR=/root/system-successor/source
install -d -m 0700 "$SOURCE_BUNDLE_DIR"
git bundle create "$SOURCE_BUNDLE_DIR/system.bundle" HEAD
git -C wizard bundle create "$SOURCE_BUNDLE_DIR/wizard.bundle" HEAD
git bundle verify "$SOURCE_BUNDLE_DIR/system.bundle"
git -C wizard bundle verify "$SOURCE_BUNDLE_DIR/wizard.bundle"
git rev-parse HEAD
```

Keep the recorded System revision and the verified bundles outside the GitLab
service. A later replacement host can clone `system.bundle`, check out that
recorded revision and initialize the Wizard without contacting GitLab or GitHub:

```bash
git clone "$SOURCE_BUNDLE_DIR/system.bundle" /opt/system
git -C /opt/system checkout --detach "$SYSTEM_TOOLS_REVISION"
git -C /opt/system \
  -c protocol.file.allow=always \
  -c submodule.wizard.url="$SOURCE_BUNDLE_DIR/wizard.bundle" \
  submodule update --init --recursive
```

Transfer the private bundles to that host first and set `SOURCE_BUNDLE_DIR` and
`SYSTEM_TOOLS_REVISION` deliberately. The file-protocol override applies only to
this invocation using the verified local bundles. These commands cover the repository's Wizard
submodule; include equivalent recorded bundles if your fork adds more submodules.
A plain source ZIP does not contain the Git objects needed by initialization.

Production promotion uses the committed operator entry point from that accepted
checkout. It must bind its actions to the reviewed source, image pins, successful
candidate results and exact existing installation. Run it from the host or an
independent management connection, rather than relying on a CI job to survive
stopping the GitLab that coordinates it.

For the declared CE 19.4.3 → 19.5.3 transition,
[`gitlab/security-release.json`](../gitlab/security-release.json) contains the
allowed image pins. Before planning or entering downtime, pull all six image
references: `fromImage`, `toImage`, `runner.fromImage`, `runner.toImage`,
`runner.fromHelperImage` and `runner.helperImage`. These include both GitLab
versions and the previous and target Runner/Helper pairs. First deploy the
**exact tested full controller image** containing the
accepted tools, while preserving the saved 19.4.3 GitLab selection. Do not rebuild
another image from the same tag and assume it has the tested identity. The helper
requires the running controller to match the image recorded by the accepted
candidate evidence; publishing a runtime base alone does not meet this condition.

#### Stage the accepted controller from the host

Check out the accepted merged source with its pinned submodules. Download these
**frozen** artifacts from its `test:platform-candidate` job:

- `test-results/successor/release.json`
- `test-results/successor/candidate-results.json`

Keep them in a private directory, for example `/root/system-successor/`, at mode
0600. Do not substitute the working `test-results/e2e/` receipt: independent cleanup
can append results there after publication, while the frozen copy's bytes are
bound to the release hash.

Provide a private token file that can read the source project's pipeline, jobs
and artifacts and pull its private registry image. Suitable `read_api` and
`read_registry` access is sufficient when the account's project permissions allow
those operations. The token value is never a command argument. The host helper
checks the configured GitLab HTTPS origin, current default-branch revision,
required successful internal jobs, exact candidate-job identity, authenticated
artifact bytes and published image/source labels. An optional GitHub mirror
failure alone is recorded separately; it does not substitute for or weaken any
internal runtime test. Other pipeline failures block promotion.

First run the source/CI input check:

```bash
sudo python3 bootstrapper/promote-controller.py \
  --operation promote \
  --persistence-env /etc/system-bootstrapper/persistence.env \
  --release /root/system-successor/release.json \
  --evidence /root/system-successor/candidate-results.json \
  --gitlab-url https://gitlab.example.com \
  --token-file /root/system-successor/gitlab-api-token \
  --checkpoint-dir /mnt/bootstrapper-data/platform/recovery/controller-promotions/REPLACE_WITH_OPERATION_ID \
  --cold-maintenance --timeout 1200 --check-only
```

Replace the origin and paths with your deployment's values. After review, run
the same command **without `--check-only`** to perform the authorized controller
promotion. `--cold-maintenance` is the bridge for an older controller whose Sync
API cannot prove the project queue is idle: the committed helper stops public
traffic, freezes the old controller with restart disabled, drains its remote
work, cleanly stops the old GitLab and takes a verified cold checkpoint before
starting the accepted controller. This is a maintenance interruption. Do not
replace this proof with an operator assertion that an old API is idle.

For a controller already supporting the required idle/lease protocol, omit
`--cold-maintenance` only when the helper accepts that protocol. Normal native
startup may reconcile NGINX and the Wizard; the acceptance condition is that
GitLab remains on the recorded old image/version and no GitLab migration has
started. The controller is selected through a source/job-specific local alias
bound to the accepted image ID. Its immutable registry reference remains release
metadata; the local alias allows a later cold start from an archive before the
platform's own registry is available.

If this **controller** operation is interrupted, use its same checkpoint with
the committed status and, when appropriate, abort actions:

```bash
sudo python3 bootstrapper/promote-controller.py \
  --operation status \
  --persistence-env /etc/system-bootstrapper/persistence.env \
  --checkpoint-dir /mnt/bootstrapper-data/platform/recovery/controller-promotions/REPLACE_WITH_OPERATION_ID

sudo python3 bootstrapper/promote-controller.py \
  --operation abort \
  --persistence-env /etc/system-bootstrapper/persistence.env \
  --checkpoint-dir /mnt/bootstrapper-data/platform/recovery/controller-promotions/REPLACE_WITH_OPERATION_ID \
  --timeout 1200
```

Inspect status before choosing an action. Controller abort verifies its owned
operation, restores the previous controller configuration and resumes the old
controller on the **same GitLab image**. It does not rewind the database and
refuses a changed GitLab image. After GitLab migration has begun, use the separate
GitLab checkpoint recovery below. The host controller tool has no `resume` action;
database rollback requires restoration through the GitLab upgrade helper.

#### Migrate GitLab through the accepted controller

Copy the frozen `candidate-results.json` privately as
`accepted-candidate-results.json` into the persistent configuration directory,
which the controller mounts at `/state`. Create a private `upgrade-options.json`
there with the following fields, replacing the example path, operation ID and
commit with your deployment's accepted values:

```json
{
  "sourceRevision": "REPLACE_WITH_ACCEPTED_40_CHARACTER_SYSTEM_COMMIT",
  "evidence": "/state/accepted-candidate-results.json",
  "stateDir": "/state",
  "persistentDir": "/mnt/bootstrapper-data/platform",
  "checkpointDir": "/state/gitlab-upgrades/REPLACE_WITH_UNIQUE_OPERATION_ID",
  "readyTimeoutSeconds": 900
}
```

Keep both input files at mode 0600. `sourceRevision` must be the exact accepted
revision in the evidence. `persistentDir` is the **host** path used by the
installation's volume bindings; `/state` and `checkpointDir` are controller paths.
Use a new checkpoint directory, with space for a full cold GitLab copy and reserve,
for each attempt. No API token is part of this options object.

From an independent host terminal, request the read-only plan:

```bash
sudo docker exec -w /system system_bootstrapper_1 \
  node gitlab/upgrade.js plan /state/upgrade-options.json
```

Inspect the returned plan and `planSha256`. It binds the accepted evidence,
source, current container and configuration to the exact old and new images and
the checkpoint location. Resolve failed preconditions before continuing; do not
edit the evidence to make a plan pass. After authorization for that exact plan,
use its hash as the confirmation:

```bash
PLAN_SHA256=REPLACE_WITH_REVIEWED_PLAN_SHA256
sudo docker exec -w /system system_bootstrapper_1 \
  node gitlab/upgrade.js promote /state/upgrade-options.json "$PLAN_SHA256"
```

Run this host command outside the GitLab CI job that will lose its server.
Retain the output, including `checkpointSha256`, privately. The checkpoint and
phase receipt are written beneath the configured `checkpointDir`; a shell or
network disconnection is not evidence that promotion succeeded or failed.

The production sequence serializes against configuration writes, Harvest/restore,
certificate-state changes and other deployments. The GitLab helper drains its HTTP
entry services before the final idle-job check, so native and external runners
cannot claim new work during checkpoint creation. If an in-flight job claim is
discovered, it restores the old HTTP service and stops before the database
shutdown/checkpoint. Otherwise, it quiesces writers, captures the final compatible
checkpoint, applies the accepted image selection, migrates and verifies B. Keep
service identity and public routing explicit. Do not enable a candidate's test
credentials or private test hostnames in Production.

After startup, verify the actual GitLab version and migration state,
authentication, repository and issue access, registry authentication and pulls,
fresh runner-manager contact, authenticated configuration Fetch, Wizard routing,
mounted storage and certificate renewal. Retain the private promotion receipt
with the accepted commit, exact image IDs/digests, checkpoint identity and check
outcomes.

#### Export B's matching recovery inputs

After GitLab migration and acceptance, run the committed recovery exporter from
the same clean accepted checkout:

```bash
sudo python3 bootstrapper/record-recovery-images.py \
  --persistence-env /etc/system-bootstrapper/persistence.env \
  --release /root/system-successor/release.json \
  --evidence /root/system-successor/candidate-results.json \
  --gitlab-url https://gitlab.example.com \
  --token-file /root/system-successor/gitlab-api-token \
  --output /root/system-successor/recovery-export.json
```

The exporter verifies the accepted CI/source evidence and running controller and
GitLab identities, writes a checksummed controller archive and updates the declared
source, aliases and public service-image selectors. It preserves previous manifest
history, versioned controller aliases and existing Wizard recovery inputs rather
than pruning them. The local controller alias is restored from its verified image
archive on the next host; no old Docker login is required to boot the registry.

Retain the export receipt and independently record its manifest checksum. Preserve
the accepted System Git objects and pinned Wizard sources outside the GitLab
service as well, especially when its optional public mirror is unavailable. Verify
the new manifest before relying on it:

```bash
sudo env PERSISTENCE_ENV_FILE=/etc/system-bootstrapper/persistence.env \
  bash bootstrapper/recover-volume.sh --verify
```

This check validates inputs without restarting services. The next
replacement host must select B's controller and GitLab images, rather than an old
manifest describing A. Keep the pre-upgrade checkpoint until B and its matching
recovery inputs have been accepted. Only then is B ready to host the next reviewed
evolution.

### 5.6 Failure, recovery and the autonomy boundary

If migration or acceptance fails, inspect the committed helper's recorded phase:

```bash
sudo docker exec -w /system system_bootstrapper_1 \
  node gitlab/upgrade.js status /state/upgrade-options.json
```

Before the helper records an accepted checkpoint hash, its `abort` action accepts
the reviewed plan hash and can recover a confirmed pre-migration failure. A
`checkpoint.json` file alone does not establish acceptance: its verification may
have failed before that hash was recorded. After checkpoint acceptance, use
`rollback` with the recorded hash to restore the compatible old state. Do not
choose between these actions from a disconnected terminal's exit code; inspect
the durable receipt and ensure no original operation is still running.

```bash
# Only for a confirmed failure before checkpoint acceptance:
sudo docker exec -w /system system_bootstrapper_1 \
  node gitlab/upgrade.js abort /state/upgrade-options.json "$PLAN_SHA256"

# For a confirmed completed-checkpoint recovery:
CHECKPOINT_SHA256=REPLACE_WITH_VERIFIED_CHECKPOINT_SHA256
sudo docker exec -w /system system_bootstrapper_1 \
  node gitlab/upgrade.js rollback /state/upgrade-options.json "$CHECKPOINT_SHA256"
```

Use only the action appropriate to the recorded phase; the commands are
alternatives, not a sequence to run unconditionally. Keep interrupted-operation
leases and incomplete-restore markers for the helper to reconcile. Do not delete
one manually to bypass a refusal.

If the controller restarted with an unfinished storage or upgrade lease and no
incomplete-restore marker, it waits in maintenance before starting writers. `docker exec` remains available
for the native status, abort or rollback commands above. It does not leave this
state automatically when recovery removes the lease. Only after the selected
recovery succeeds and its barriers are released, resume controller startup:

```bash
sudo docker restart system_bootstrapper_1
```

If GitLab is restored to the old image while an accepted controller remains
staged, develop any correction through a new merge request and its required
checks. Use the documented [staged-controller replacement](../bootstrapper/README.md#replacing-an-accepted-controller-before-gitlab-migration)
with the previous completed controller checkpoint and a new operation directory.
The tool authenticates the prior candidate separately while keeping the new
candidate's current-default-branch gates strict. Do not edit saved selectors or
the old recovery manifest to make the replacement pass.

If the target GitLab has started, stop its writers and preserve the failure receipt. Do not simply start the old
GitLab image on a database already migrated by B. Recovery requires the compatible
pre-upgrade state, configuration/secrets and exact old images through the
committed recovery procedure. Keep the failed
candidate data separate until diagnosis is complete; do not overwrite the only
usable checkpoint. See [Harvest/Seed recovery](RECOVERY_CONTRACT.md) for the cold
snapshot contract and incomplete-restore guard.

The platform automates the declared, tested sequence. It does not grant an agent
permission to invent new infrastructure changes, bypass review or weaken merge
gates. In this chapter, autonomous execution means carrying out the authorized
version transition and its verification using repository-owned tools. Choosing
arbitrary improvements and recursively promoting them without acceptance remains
a separate capability that must not be inferred from a successful patch upgrade.

# Use GitLab as primary with an optional GitHub code mirror

The guarded backup helper forwards a protected GitLab default-branch commit
to an explicitly mapped GitHub branch. It is opt-in: adding the helper to a
checkout does not change remotes, activate synchronization or migrate project
metadata. Select a primary repository and integrate the helper into its chosen
CI configuration before enabling it.

## Development and tracking roles

Select the GitLab projects for System and Wizard and a central issue tracker.
An operator may keep their issues together in the System project while reviewing
Wizard changes in the Wizard project. Record the selected identities in agent
instructions and external project tracking; the product does not require one
maintainer's GitLab host or issue history.

After activation, create work in that GitLab tracker, branch from the intended
GitLab default branch, and open the merge request in the affected source project.
Reference cross-project issues with their project-qualified GitLab reference.
Run the project's required checks, review the final diff and merge there. The
protected default-branch pipeline then forwards that exact merged commit to the
mapped GitHub branch. GitHub is a public code mirror, not a second merge target.
Contributors and agents use the same issue, branch, review and merge workflow.

GitHub availability is not a prerequisite for source checks, merge-request work
or private delivery. If the enabled mirror job fails, its pipeline remains
visibly failed and the job is retryable. Required source-check evidence and
delivery evidence remain independently usable; do not hide the mirror failure
with `allow_failure` or require that job to succeed before continuing internal
work. Configure merge permissions and required source checks accordingly.

A successful mirror job does not promote Production. In particular, Wizard
Production remains a separate deliberate action using verified pipeline, source
and immutable image evidence. Moving development does not extend the Wizard's
existing rollout mechanism into automatic deployment of the whole platform.

## Resolve history before enabling anything

Record an explicit mapping for both System and Wizard:

| Setting | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Source project | Exact GitLab `owner/project` identity |
| Source branch | The project's protected GitLab default branch |
| Backup repository | Existing `git@github.com:owner/repository.git` |
| Backup branch | Explicit destination; it need not share the source branch name |

A Wizard initialized through the managed source-import workflow starts with
scaffold/import commits, rather than the upstream GitHub ancestry. Such a
repository cannot simply fast-forward the existing upstream branch. Review
either a history-preserving migration into GitLab or a separate backup branch
with an agreed starting point. The same ancestry check applies to any source
and destination pair. Do not force-push, synthesize an automatic merge or
quietly switch the backup target. The helper requires an existing destination
branch with compatible ancestry.

### Source projects and managed delivery projects

If the managed Wizard repository has independent private history, a clean
source-primary project can preserve the public source ancestry while the
existing managed repository continues to build and deliver the application.
These are distinct roles, even when both projects live in the same GitLab.
Keep managed delivery history private: merging its ancestors into a public
source branch would publish those commits too, even if the resulting files
look identical. Retain the existing project, refs, receipts, managed recipes
and deployment generation floors when establishing the clean source project.

The source-to-delivery handoff is explicit and reviewed. For the accepted merged
`sourceCommit`, verify that the required `build:source` and `test:browser` jobs
succeeded for that exact SHA. Record those job identities, the source SHA,
current delivery base and resulting `deliveryCommit` in external tracking or
private operator records. Overall pipeline success is not the source gate:
an optional GitHub mirror outage can leave the pipeline failed while those
required jobs succeeded. No GitHub read or mirror-job success is required for
the private delivery build, its tests or the reviewed handoff.

Transfer only the reviewed application
changes from that source commit, inspect any differing destination files, and
use the destination's normal branch/MR process or guarded managed operation.
Never replace its managed CI, ownership markers or history by reimporting the
whole source tree to bypass a conflict. Verify the transferred files against
the selected source revision and run the delivery build and browser tests.
Production proof identifies the actual delivery commit and image digest;
the handoff mapping links it to the reviewed source commit. This procedure
does not imply an automatic source-to-delivery synchronizer or automatic
System deployment.

Keep the upstream public submodule URL portable. Inside a GitLab-primary System
checkout, explicitly select the matching private Wizard source before updating:

```sh
git config submodule.wizard.url '<operator-selected GitLab Wizard clone URL>'
git submodule update --init wizard
```

Use an authenticated clone URL without embedded credentials. `git submodule
sync` replaces a local override with `.gitmodules`, so reapply the private
mapping if syncing is needed. In System CI, `prepare:wizard-source` disables
automatic runner submodule checkout with `GIT_SUBMODULE_STRATEGY: none`.
`gitlab/prepare-wizard-source.js` then initializes and verifies the exact gitlink
using the configured private selector before source packaging. An override
applied only after this preparation step would be too late.
Verify that the selected Wizard repository contains the exact System gitlink.
The development and test path must not need a successful GitHub read to proceed.

## Helper contract

`gitlab/github-backup.sh` runs in a checkout with an `origin` pointing to the
intended primary GitLab project. The CI integration provides its pinned Node 24
runtime, Git, OpenSSH client/agent and a POSIX shell with `mkdir` and `rmdir`.
Keep the companion
`github-backup-transport.js` beside the shell helper. Configuration comes from
the protected CI job:

| Variable | Required value |
| --- | --- |
| `GITHUB_BACKUP_ENABLED` | `true` to explicitly enable the configured backup job |
| `GITHUB_BACKUP_SOURCE_PROJECT` | Approved exact `CI_PROJECT_PATH` |
| `GITHUB_BACKUP_REMOTE` | Approved GitHub SSH repository, without credentials |
| `GITHUB_BACKUP_BRANCH` | Approved existing backup branch |
| `GITHUB_BACKUP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | Optional per-transport deadline, integer 1–300; default 30 |
| `GITHUB_SSH_KNOWN_HOSTS` | Protected file variable containing independently verified GitHub SSH host keys |

GitLab supplies `GITLAB_CI`, `CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE`, `CI_PROJECT_PATH`,
`CI_DEFAULT_BRANCH`, `CI_COMMIT_BRANCH`, `CI_COMMIT_REF_PROTECTED` and
`CI_COMMIT_SHA`. Only a protected default-branch **push** pipeline is eligible.
MR, API, manual/web and tag pipelines do not replicate. The checkout must match
the full pinned SHA, and that commit must still belong to the freshly fetched
source default branch. Configure protected-branch permissions so only reviewed
merges reach it; a shell script cannot prove that review took place.

The helper fetches complete source ancestry, including unshallowing CI clones.
The runner therefore needs read access to the primary and write access to the
mapped backup. It changes neither `origin`, the checkout, nor local branches.
Temporary refs under `refs/system-backup/` are removed on normal exit/signals.
Those scratch refs are replaceable; the destination branch is never force-pushed.

Each invocation forwards the **same merged commit**, using a normal Git push:

- A target behind the pinned commit advances by fast-forward only.
- An equal target is an idempotent success.
- A target already containing an older queued commit succeeds without rewinding.
- A divergent target, missing branch or removed source commit fails visibly.
- Rejected pushes and uncertain responses are re-fetched and re-evaluated, with
  at most three push attempts. Retry the CI job after resolving an access error.

Push explicitly disables inherited `push.followTags`; only the configured
branch is forwarded. Each fetch/push runs under the Node transport boundary
with a wall-clock deadline. On Unix it owns a process group, sends TERM and
then KILL after two seconds even if the leader exited first. On Windows the
offline fixture targets only its own recorded child PID/tree using `taskkill`.
Cancellation uses the same tree cleanup. The CI job must retain a finite job
timeout with runner process cleanup as an outer safety boundary. A deadline
failure releases the checkout lock; an uncatchable host/process termination
still requires the interrupted-owner inspection described below.

A checkout-local lock rejects overlapping invocations using the same Git object
database. An uncatchable termination can leave that lock behind; inspect the
owner before removing `.git/system-github-backup.lock` (use the common Git
directory for linked worktrees). **This is not a distributed lock.** The CI job
must also use the same per-repository `resource_group` across eligible pipelines.
Normal Git ref updates remain atomic even if two independent checkouts race.
An older job can run after a newer one safely. See
[GitLab resource groups](https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/resource_groups/).

The helper suppresses transport output, disables shell tracing and local Git
hooks, and logs only fixed outcome messages. Transport output is discarded,
terminal/credential-manager prompts are disabled and SSH uses BatchMode with
strict host-key checking. The job must pre-provision verified `known_hosts`;
unknown keys fail rather than prompt or bypass verification. The core helper
does not read a private-key variable, print a remote URL or install credentials.
The CI wrapper reads the selected private key and starts an owned temporary
SSH agent. That setup must use protected/masked credentials and verified host
keys; do not enable
CI debug tracing or echo secrets in surrounding commands. Retain the existing
protected `GITHUB_SSH_PRIVATE_KEY` identity unless separately authorized.

## Integrate with the selected CI configuration

System's `deploy:github` job uses this helper after its required checks. It is
explicitly opt-in and uses the selected default branch, supported pinned Node
runtime, verified `GITHUB_SSH_KNOWN_HOSTS` file and existing protected SSH identity.
Configure all mapped values before enabling it. The job is serialized by
`github-backup-$CI_PROJECT_ID`; its failure remains a failed pipeline result.

System's `build` job publishes the standalone runtime base to its own GitLab
registry as `$CI_REGISTRY_IMAGE:$CI_COMMIT_REF_SLUG` after the required runtime
checks. The complete successor controller is published separately by the
candidate acceptance job to the same project's `/successor` repository, with
an immutable digest and acceptance evidence. Follow the
[successor promotion guide](../bootstrapper/README.md#promoting-a-tested-successor-controller)
to deploy that complete image. Neither publication requires Docker Hub publishing
credentials, enables Production promotion or bypasses the resource-heavy System
candidate checks. GitHub mirroring remains independently opt-in.

The legacy managed Wizard selects `.system-bootstrapper/ci.yml` for build/test and any
installed optional environment jobs. Its preserved upstream `.gitlab-ci.yml`
is not active. A source-primary repository uses the committed
`.gitlab/primary.yml` instead. It always runs `build:source` (locked install,
lint, unit tests, TypeScript, production build and configuration-export bundle)
and `test:browser` against that exact build artifact using Playwright Chromium
and a loopback preview. These two source checks need no host Docker access.

With `WIZARD_DELIVERY_ENABLED=true`, that same source-primary pipeline also runs
required `build:wizard` and `test:wizard` jobs using its committed generic build
recipe. Those jobs require a trusted Docker runner, publish the immutable image
in the same project's registry and verify that exact image. Configured optional
Review/Beta jobs then use the same project; Production remains a separate
controlled promotion. Follow the [source-primary adoption guide](../project-bootstrap/wizard-source-primary/README.md)
when replacing an existing managed delivery project. Do not delete the old
project until its live dependencies and required recovery data are migrated.

Installations retaining separate source and delivery projects can leave this
flag unset. Keep their private delivery project's managed CI path and recipe
unchanged. Do not enable the preserved upstream pipeline merely to obtain its
legacy publishing jobs.

Only the eligible protected default-branch pipeline reaches `deploy:github`.
The publisher retains its protected enablement gate, serialized resource group
and visible failure result. Source-primary delivery verifies all required
native source/image checks independently: a pending, running, failed or canceled
public mirror alone does not prevent private environment or Production promotion. Source
merges still respect the project's successful-pipeline and discussion gates.

Use the existing protected `GITHUB_SSH_PRIVATE_KEY` identity; a file variable is
preferred, while existing masked multiline values remain supported. Supply SSH
host keys in `GITHUB_SSH_KNOWN_HOSTS` after independent verification, never a
runtime key scan. System CI can use `WIZARD_PRIMARY_REPOSITORY_URL` to fetch its
exact gitlink from the operator-selected Wizard project on the same HTTPS
origin as `CI_SERVER_URL`, using the job token. Authorize the System project to
read that Wizard project through GitLab's job-token permissions. The URL is a
nonsecret selector and must also be available to ordinary MR pipelines; making
only this variable protected would leave those pipelines on the public fallback.
The job token remains process-local and redirects are refused. The public
`.gitmodules` mapping remains available for fresh public recursive checkouts.
Before fetching, the source selector reconciles an existing or reinitialized
Wizard submodule's cached `remote.origin.url` to the chosen credential-free
internal URL, then verifies the exact gitlink. A previously cached public remote
therefore cannot silently override the selected internal source. The System
superproject's `origin` remains unchanged.

The upstream Wizard also has `deploy:system`, which updates the System gitlink
and uses a legacy hardcoded GitLab host. Do not reactivate it blindly. The
internal order is Wizard merge/checks and exact commit availability in the
GitLab source project, then a deliberate System gitlink update and System checks
through the normal review process. Public mirroring has a separate restoration
ordering: ensure the referenced Wizard commit is present on its GitHub mirror
before claiming the System mirror supports a fresh public recursive checkout.
A lagging public mirror does not block internal gitlink work or private delivery.
No automatic System merge
or Production deployment is introduced. Production remains a deliberate
operator-confirmed [promotion action](../project-bootstrap/wizard-production/README.md).

### Deliver the Wizard in one System release

An explicitly selected alternative bundles interface and System changes into one
System merge request. Retain the reviewed Wizard commit on a dedicated source
ref, pin that exact gitlink in the System MR, and include its complete comparison
in the review. This does not advance the Wizard's default branch or manufacture
native Wizard pipeline evidence. The System pipeline runs the Wizard's source
and browser checks, full platform acceptance and both-image publication together.
The merged default branch receives its own required checks. No intermediate
System pipeline or second Wizard pipeline is needed for this path.

For public recursive checkouts, enable these additional **protected** System CI
variables alongside the normal GitHub mirror configuration:

| Variable | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `WIZARD_GITHUB_SOURCE_PUBLISH_ENABLED` | `true` to publish the exact dependency before the System mirror |
| `WIZARD_GITHUB_BACKUP_REMOTE` | GitHub SSH destination matching the committed Wizard `.gitmodules` HTTPS URL |
| `WIZARD_GITHUB_SSH_PRIVATE_KEY` | File variable with an authorized Wizard-repository publishing identity |

Use the Wizard repository's authorized publishing identity; a System deploy key
does not imply access to another repository. The existing independently verified
GitHub host-key file must also apply to that destination. The wrapper keeps the
two identities separate and removes its private copies and SSH agent on exit.

`gitlab/publish-wizard-source.js` reads the exact gitlink from the protected
System default-branch push, obtains it from the same-instance canonical Wizard
source with the job token, and publishes `system-release/<Wizard commit>`.
An atomic create-only lease refuses changing an existing ref, including an
ancestor. Retrying verifies the same commit. The helper fetches that exact ref
anonymously from the public HTTPS repository before the ordinary System mirror
runs. Neither Wizard default branch is changed. Retain these source refs while
a published release or recovery input needs them.

The same-pipeline `test-results/github/wizard-source.json` receipt records only
source, destination and job identities. The opt-in
[paired release updater](../bootstrapper/README.md#deliberately-updating-the-accepted-controller-and-wizard-together)
requires this successful publication proof, the full accepted System pipeline
and the unchanged Docker Hub image-pair artifact. Its default controller-only
mode keeps the original mirror policy. Production promotion remains deliberate;
the source-primary Wizard binding and its ordinary native promotion rules remain
separate and unchanged.

## Activate the selected primary/backup relationship

1. Verify the real GitLab review, required-check and deployment workflow on your
   own infrastructure before changing its role.
2. Agree mappings and resolve the history prerequisite above. Preserve previous
   refs and record a rollback contact/procedure. Pause competing writes during
   the switch; GitHub becomes backup-only, not another merge destination.
3. Audit GitHub Actions, deployments, webhooks and reverse mirrors. Disable or
   explicitly isolate reactions to backup pushes **before** activation. A
   byte-identical commit cannot be given a new skip marker without changing its
   identity. Audit the Wizard-to-System job separately to prevent a return loop.
4. Deliberately update remotes, agent guidance and issue/MR handling to the new
   primary. Transfer active work using the procedure below; Git pushes do not
   move issue metadata. Issue migration is separate from this helper.
5. Review and enable only the intended protected backup jobs, using authorized
   credentials and verified known-host material. Run the offline regressions
   before an explicitly controlled integration check.
6. Merge a harmless GitLab change through the reviewed workflow. Compare the exact
   resulting SHA on GitHub, test a visible failure/retry, and verify that no return push or
   unintended deployment occurred. Keep the former workflow recoverable until
   a disposable restore rehearsal passes.

## Transfer active work without losing its origin

Inventory active issues and pull requests before changing the tracker. Include
the original repository identity, item type/number, URL, title, description,
state, labels, ownership, timestamps, relevant discussion and acceptance
criteria. Keep that inventory, old-to-new identifiers and cutover verification
in external tracking or private operator records, not source documentation.
Never include tokens, private logs or deployment credentials in an issue export.

For each active issue, search the destination for its exact original URL before
creating a replacement. Put that URL and original identity in the new item's
description, preserve its requirements, and attribute copied comments to their
original author and timestamp rather than presenting them as new statements by
the importer. Validate the resulting text and links. Record the destination URL
back on the old item before closing it as moved. Retry by the recorded mapping
and source identity, so an interrupted transfer does not create duplicates.

Closed historical discussions may remain readable in the old tracker. Record
that choice explicitly; a Git source mirror does not migrate that history.
Retain an operator export if those records must remain accessible without the
old service. Already merged commits and historical commit messages need no
rewriting to replace old issue references. New discussions use the selected
GitLab tracker. Disable new issue creation and competing merge paths on the
mirror when supported, and publish the new contribution destination externally.

An open pull request requires its branch, target and review state to be checked
separately before recreating a GitLab merge request. Original reviews are
historical context, not fresh approval of a changed diff. Do not import a branch
by overwriting managed files or rewriting the destination's existing history.

## Verify the cutover on operator-owned infrastructure

Use a harmless change and private verification records for each source project:

1. Create a GitLab issue with a unique marker. Make a branch and merge request
   referring to it; for Wizard, verify the cross-project central issue link.
   Check that agents can read the issue and submit/review the merge request.
2. Prove an MR pipeline cannot publish the code mirror and a required-check
   failure cannot pass the merge/delivery gate. Review and merge the corrected
   diff through the protected branch's intended permissions.
3. Record the resulting full GitLab commit SHA. Confirm the eligible default-
   branch pipeline succeeds and GitHub contains that exact commit, without
   synthetic merge commits, reverse pushes or Production changes. Compare the
   final branch tip when no newer merges are queued; older queued jobs must
   not rewind a destination that already contains their commit.
4. Re-run the mirror job to prove idempotence. Exercise denied write access in
   an isolated mapping with a dedicated test credential, confirm visible
   failure, restore access and retry. Never break a shared production key or
   manufacture divergent history on the public branch for this test.
5. For System, verify GitLab-primary checkout with its internal submodule mapping.
   Confirm its required work and private Wizard delivery can run while GitHub is
   unavailable, using exact successful required-job evidence rather than overall
   pipeline success; the enabled mirror job remains visibly failed until retry.
   After the referenced Wizard commit is mirrored, verify fresh public recursive
   checkout separately before reporting the public System mirror restore-ready.
6. Capture a completed Harvest and matching configuration export using the
   existing recovery contract. In a disposable restoration, verify the fixture
   user, repository head, issue description marker, draft MR/discussion metadata and an
   encrypted CI setting, then execute a runner job. Keep restored mirror writes
   disabled until the recovered state and mappings have been reviewed.

The committed cold recovery scenario creates a source branch and draft MR with
a discussion and reply, in addition to its user, repository/issue identity,
encrypted CI variable and registry data. It checks the exact source commit,
MR identity, title, description, state, author and creation time, plus both
notes' identities, text, authors, timestamps and resolution state after restore.
The issue check compares its description marker, not its title or state. The MR
stays open with null merge-commit/time fields, so this is not proof of restoring
an already merged MR. The fixture leaves the default branch unchanged. Offline
contract success alone does not establish a passed real cold restore, live
cutover or a successful Production rollout; run the
[disposable recovery scenario](../tests/e2e/README.md) on sufficient capacity.

## Coverage and restore limits

The helper backs up one configured branch and reachable Git objects. It does
not mirror tags, other branches, deletions, Git LFS payloads or submodule
repositories; define those policies explicitly before claiming wider coverage.
It does not back up issues, MRs, discussions, users, CI secrets, registry images,
artifacts or service configuration.

The platform's existing [persistent volume](PERSISTENT_VOLUME.md) and
[cold Harvest/Seed recovery](RECOVERY_CONTRACT.md) handle service state separately
from this code mirror. GitLab's retained `config` and `data` trees include its
configuration/secrets, database, repositories and local registry/artifact data.
Issues, MR discussions, users and CI settings depend on that GitLab state, not
just Git commits. Harvest captures these trees while GitLab is cleanly stopped;
the separate Wizard configuration export supplies Bootstrapper settings. A
retained live volume can also be reused without applying an older Seed.

No second backup service is required by selecting GitLab as primary. Review any
operator-configured external object storage against the Seed's actual local
coverage. Protect secret material and preserve the matching version/edition
and image identity required by the recovery contract. Review the installation's
[backup coverage](https://docs.gitlab.com/administration/backup_restore/backup_gitlab/)
and [restore prerequisites](https://docs.gitlab.com/administration/backup_restore/restore_gitlab/),
then rehearse on an isolated disposable system. The branch-forwarding helper
does not run Harvest/Seed or GitLab-native backup/restore operations.

## Offline regression checks

Run `node tests/gitlab/github-backup.js` where Git and a POSIX `sh` are available.
On Windows, set `GITHUB_BACKUP_TEST_SHELL` to Git for Windows' `usr/bin/sh.exe`.
The fixture creates and removes only its own temporary local repositories.
`GITHUB_BACKUP_OFFLINE_FIXTURE=1` permits an existing absolute local bare target
instead of GitHub SSH; it is only for those offline fixtures, never production CI.
The fixture exercises exact-SHA forwarding, retries, out-of-order commits,
eligibility guards, divergence, missing history, lock contention, competing
checkouts, inherited tag configuration, hanging transport descendants,
cancellation and secret-output suppression. It never contacts a remote service.

# Initialize the Wizard repository from pinned source

This is the legacy managed-source workflow. An explicitly adopted
[source-primary repository](../project-bootstrap/wizard-source-primary/README.md)
develops directly through its own merge requests and does not import source.
Generic `.system-bootstrapper/build-v1/` producers committed by such a repository
are excluded from legacy source snapshots: managed build activation installs its
own reviewed recipe in that reserved namespace.

The registered Wizard project represents the existing interface. Source
initialization is a separate, explicit operation; automatic registration,
startup, Fetch and configuration Push never import application source.

## Use the action

1. Run matching System and Wizard versions, complete default Wizard registration,
   connect to Sync and Fetch the project list.
2. Expand the managed Wizard project and choose **Initialize Wizard source**.
3. Check the repository, source revision and file count in the preview.
4. Select **Import source**. The authenticated asynchronous operation reports
   completion or an actionable conflict. Closing and reopening the dialog allows
   a retry after an interrupted request.

Only the private repository created by this instance's registration is accepted.
Its ownership marker, identity, default branch and disabled managed CI must
match. New source paths and a provenance marker are committed atomically with
`[skip ci]`. Existing paths are never overwritten. Retrying verifies matching
content, executable modes and import commit evidence before reporting success.
A maintainer edit requires inspection rather than a destructive reset.

The scaffold README remains unchanged. The original source README is placed at
`.system-bootstrapper/SOURCE_README.md`. The original upstream `.gitlab-ci.yml`
is preserved byte-for-byte, but GitLab's CI path continues to point at the
disabled `.system-bootstrapper/ci.yml`. No pipeline is started. The known safe
`SKIP_PREFLIGHT_CHECK=true` value is supplied separately under
`.system-bootstrapper/preflight.env`; local dotenv files are excluded.

The running interface, routing and Production URL are untouched. Beta and Review
remain disabled. Source initialization does not start builds or deployment;
[managed build activation](WIZARD_BUILD.md) is a separate explicit action.
Review/Beta deployment and
[Production promotion](../project-bootstrap/wizard-production/README.md) are
separate explicit operations. Importing source does not promote an image.

## Build the immutable source package

Initialize the pinned Wizard submodule before building the System image:

```sh
git submodule update --init wizard
bash project-bootstrap/wizard-source/prepare.sh
```

The normal root `start.sh` invokes preparation before Compose builds the System
image. Manual System image builds must run the same command first. The image
build validates the generated manifest and file hashes; it fails if preparation
was omitted. Do not commit the generated `snapshot.json`.

Preparation reads Git objects at the Wizard gitlink committed in the System's
HEAD. Dirty checkout files, untracked files and a different checked-out Wizard
branch cannot change the snapshot. It preserves binary bytes and executable
modes, rejects symlinks and nested submodules, and excludes dotenv files,
credential file conventions, seeds, dependency directories and build outputs.
Review committed application source as usual; filename filtering is not a
secret scanner for arbitrary source code.

Node on the host is optional. If unavailable, preparation builds the reviewed
`bootstrapper` runtime recipe as `system-bootstrapper-source-tools:local`, then
runs its Node/Git tools with network disabled and source/Git-object mounts
read-only. Linked Git worktrees require their referenced metadata directories
to remain accessible. No Docker socket is mounted in the packaging container.

## State and recovery

The existing private Wizard project configuration contains the versioned
`wizardWorkflow` receipt: operation, source revision, manifest hash, phase,
import commit and safe failure message. Registration and repository identity
are preserved. Existing server-owned project preservation carries the complete
receipt across Push and restart. Retry inspects the repository after a lost
response rather than issuing another import commit. Source revision upgrades
after a reserved import require a separate reviewed operation.

If the source snapshot is missing, prepare it and rebuild the matching System
image. For ownership, path or CI conflicts, inspect the repository and local
registration first. Do not delete/recreate a repository or reset credentials to
make initialization pass.

## Isolated verification

After compiling Sync and generating the snapshot, run:

```sh
node tests/wizard/source-package.js
node tests/wizard/source-workflow.js
ruby tests/wizard/source-import.rb
```

The package test creates disposable Git repositories. The workflow test uses a
temporary private configuration and stubbed Rails transport. The Ruby adapter
test uses an in-memory GitLab API fixture. These tests never contact the running
GitLab or mutate the platform. Run the Wizard checks with the Node/npm versions
declared in `wizard/package.json`: `npm ci`, `npm run lint`, `npm test`,
`npm run build` and `npm run test:config-export`. The managed build recipe selects
the matching source toolchain profile; historical reservations retain their
exact recipe hashes.
