# Build and verify the imported Wizard

Managed CI activation builds and verifies a candidate after
[source initialization](WIZARD_SOURCE.md). Build activation preserves the running
Wizard. Review/Beta use separate
[manual environment jobs](../project-bootstrap/wizard-environments/README.md);
Production uses the guarded [operator promotion command](../project-bootstrap/wizard-production/README.md).

## Preview and activate

For the complete browser procedure, see
[Build and check the Wizard manually](HANDBOOK.md#build-and-check-the-wizard-manually).
The prerequisites include a prepared source package in the matching System
image, the registered managed project, an available project registry, and a
reviewed runner accepting the `docker` tag with Docker/Buildx and registry
access. Check physical disk/RAM headroom before starting; this workflow builds
application and browser images and should not compete with other infrastructure
builds on a constrained host. No additional project runner is required when the
shared runner already meets these conditions.

Use matching System/Wizard versions, complete source initialization and configure
the platform's GitLab registry. Connect to Sync, Fetch the managed project and
expand its row. Choose **Build and verify Wizard** to inspect the owned
repository, imported commit and managed recipe version.

Opening this preview changes no repository files or pipelines. **Enable build
pipeline** explicitly confirms the previewed recipe hash. The asynchronous
operation installs the separate managed recipe, preserves upstream publishing
files and starts or recovers the recorded initial pipeline. Production remains
unchanged. Closing a pending preview is safe; dismissal is disabled during the
activation request. **Refresh status** retrieves the recorded pipeline/checks
through the same job polling contract.

## Status and safe continuation

| State | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Activation reserved / recipe installed | Refresh status, or review a fresh preview and explicitly resume activation. |
| Pipeline running | Inspect the pipeline or refresh status later. |
| Required checks failed | Inspect or retry the failed jobs in GitLab, then refresh the same operation. |
| Candidate verified | The controller has verified required checks and matching immutable artifact evidence; Production is unchanged. |
| Pipeline outcome requires reconciliation | Refresh only. An administrator must inspect the durable operation/checkpoint and GitLab before repair. Never clear the checkpoint blindly. |
| Verification failed | Prior artifact claims are hidden. Inspect the error and refresh; review a fresh preview before explicitly resuming when safe. |

**Resume activation** is offered only for pending, recipe-installed or
verification-failed state after a fresh preview. A status request or failure
invalidates the previous preview confirmation; **Refresh preview** obtains a new
one. The server's ownership, expected-content and durable pipeline checks remain
authoritative. A button does not bypass them. Uncertain creation never offers a
second blind activation.

The image reference is displayed only for `candidate-verified`, not merely a
successful pipeline status or a previously cached artifact. Failed verification
hides it immediately. Ordinary source import must not be used to upgrade an
already enabled build recipe.

## Inspect the pipeline and candidate evidence

Use **Open pipeline** in the dialog to inspect the recorded operation rather
than starting a new pipeline from GitLab. The managed CI configuration is
`.system-bootstrapper/ci.yml`; the preserved upstream `.gitlab-ci.yml` is not
activated by this action.

| Job | Work and evidence |
| --- | --- |
| `build:wizard` | Installs the committed lockfile, runs the selected toolchain checks, publishes the candidate, and records the source commit, pipeline ID and immutable registry digest in `build-evidence.json`. |
| `test:wizard` | Pulls that immutable image, checks HTTP and browser rendering/Projects/SPA navigation, then records matching identity in `wizard-evidence.json`; `browser-evidence/` contains browser results and a screenshot. |

Each job has a 30-minute timeout. The configured artifact retention is seven
days. A browser screenshot alone does not verify the source/image identity, and
a successful image push alone does not prove the browser checks passed. Both
required jobs and their matching artifact claims must verify before the
controller displays **Verified candidate image**. The reference uses
`registry/repository@sha256:…`; a mutable tag is not equivalent evidence.

Refresh status after a job retry in the same pipeline. Do not manufacture a
replacement artifact or clear the operation checkpoint after evidence expires
or verification fails. Inspect the reported error and use only the guarded
continuation offered by a fresh preview, or request administrator reconciliation.
Record the pipeline/commit/image identity when retaining acceptance evidence;
keep configuration, credentials and tokens out of reports.

The build recipe has build and test stages only. Installing the separate
environment recipe adds manual Review/Beta jobs. Neither recipe enables a
Production deployment job; Production promotion requires an explicit operator
plan and confirmation.

## Controller API

All routes require the existing Sync bearer authentication:

| Route | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /projects/wizard/build` | Read-only repository/source/recipe preview and saved build state. |
| `POST /projects/wizard/build` | Explicit `{recipeHash}` activation; returns an asynchronous job. |
| `GET /projects/wizard/build/status` | Safe asynchronous refresh, or `not-activated` without creating a pipeline. |
| `GET /projects/jobs/:id` | Existing polling endpoint; completion returns `{build,message}`. |

Runner/startup operations and other project mutations are guarded. Repeated
requests for this build's own active operation return its existing job. Status
refresh does not install files or create pipelines.

## Toolchain profiles

New source imports with Vite select the `node24-vite8-ca-v4` profile: the
pinned Node 24/npm toolchain, locked install, lint, Vitest, TypeScript/Vite build,
configuration-export checks and Playwright browser checks. Browser evidence
includes rendered UI, Projects, SPA navigation, a configuration ZIP and exact
Cube validation. Use `wizard/package.json` and the managed recipe for the exact
pinned versions.

This profile retains the overview browser checks and exact-tag cleanup, and
refreshes the build/browser images' public CA trust from the reviewed, checksummed
Mozilla bundle shipped with the System source. Node uses that refreshed OpenSSL
trust store. The refresh runs while building or preparing job images, without
downloading a new trust bundle at runtime or changing the host's trust store.

The inherited overview checks verify **Getting Started**, Overview/Wizard switching,
preserved workspace selection and the **Open Wizard** action when those controls
are present; earlier modern source keeps its direct-workspace checks. To deliver
the new navigation from an existing managed project, first perform its guarded
build/environment-only upgrade with the explicit private option
`"buildProfile": "node24-vite8-ca-v4"`. Existing overview, cleanup-v2 and earlier
profiles retain their exact historical hashes. The equivalent current legacy
profile is `legacy-ca-v4`.

Reserved historical recipes remain verifiable by their exact hash, including
legacy Node 13/CRA/Jest recipes. Historical compatibility does not make that
obsolete toolchain appropriate for a new project. Upgrading an imported
project requires the guarded [source/toolchain migration](../project-bootstrap/wizard-upgrade/README.md);
changing a controller image does not rewrite an existing reservation. A
build/environment-only upgrade is available when source is already modern and
must retain local development.
An existing recipe reservation is not silently refreshed by a controller
upgrade; use the explicit versioned migration to rebuild its affected job images.

## Verification

The isolated API, recipe and adapter fixtures check explicit confirmation,
continuation, failure/status presentation, ownership and mutation guards:

```sh
node tests/wizard/build-recipe.js
node tests/wizard/build-workflow.js
ruby tests/gitlab/wizard-build.rb
```

These fixtures do not contact the running GitLab. Complete integration checks
also need a real owned project, successful required jobs, matching immutable
registry artifacts, browser evidence and job-owned resource cleanup. Inspect
actual pipeline results before promotion; a candidate artifact alone is not a
Production rollout. Keep tokens and private configuration out of reports.

chapters.outcome: Required build/browser evidence verifies an immutable candidate image without promoting Production.

chapters.markdown:
# Managed Wizard Review and Beta

The environment workflow extends the managed source/build receipts. Production promotion and rollback remain
outside this recipe. The existing public source CI and publishing destinations
are retained.

Review uses one exact HTTPS host and a single active merge-request lease.
The resource identity includes the project and MR IID. A different MR must wait
until the current Review is stopped; a newer verified pipeline of the same MR
may replace it. Beta uses a separate exact host and the current default-branch
head. Deploy and Stop are manual native GitLab jobs for both environments.
There are no Production jobs or arbitrary image deployment endpoints.

## Configuration and installation

The authenticated Wizard environment dialog previews optional settings. Each
enabled row requires an explicit exact host, domain mode 2 and certificate/key
paths under /ssl. Wildcard domain modes are unsupported in this recipe. Disabled
rows may be blank. Settings are not inferred and enabled automatically.

The server validates DNS against the current Production host addresses, exact
certificate coverage, validity and matching private key. Reserve the hosts
separately from platform and other project routes. Provision their certificates
before confirming installation. Existing Production settings and the immutable
System Cube, including its fixed HTTPS www URL and port 8071, remain unchanged.

A confirmed preview installs versioned managed files and the selected CI through
one guarded skip-CI commit. It does not start a pipeline or deploy a container.
Unexpected edits, occupied paths, changed previews and ownership mismatches
fail closed. Refresh inspects the same operation without creating another
commit or pipeline. An uncertain commit outcome requires reconciliation before
retrying. A verified installed operation is ready for the manual CI jobs.

To change settings, stop active environments and reconcile pending work first.
Preview again and explicitly confirm the change. The update checks the prior
recipe and exact file identities before replacing managed content. Preserve the
server-owned receipt across Fetch/Push and controller startup. Earlier build
evidence remains historical; use environment status for the installed recipe.

## Immutable helper provisioning

The operator must build a clean System image from the tested committed source
and its matching validated Wizard snapshot. Do not include private configuration,
credentials, Git metadata or host runtime output. Provision that image on the
existing runner Docker daemon, retain it while the recipe is installed, and
configure SYSTEM_WIZARD_ENVIRONMENT_IMAGE with its exact sha256 image ID.
SYSTEM_WIZARD_CANONICAL_CONTROLLER must identify system_bootstrapper_1.
The UI cannot choose a helper image or canonical controller.

From the matching System checkout with initialized submodules, prepare the pinned
source package before building the complete helper image:

```sh
bash project-bootstrap/wizard-source/prepare.sh
docker build -f system/Dockerfile -t system-wizard-helper:local .
docker image inspect --format '{{.Id}}' system-wizard-helper:local
```

Record that returned image ID in the private controller configuration and make
that exact image available on the runner's Docker daemon. The standalone runtime
base is not the complete helper. See [source packaging](../../docs/WIZARD_SOURCE.md)
for the pinned snapshot contract.

CI uses ordinary job-scoped registry credentials to preload its candidate
digest. No Sync/admin credential enters the helper. The helper uses the existing
trusted Docker runner model and the original controller/GitLab containers for
canonical receipt and job checks. This is not isolation for hostile repository
code. The helper is bounded and uses network none, a read-only root filesystem,
the existing Docker socket, templates volume and read-only SSL volume; it does
not receive a new configuration volume.

The exact running job, pipeline, source head, MR identity, selected CI and
successful required build/browser artifacts are checked server-side before
deployment. Temporary verification access remains inside GitLab and is revoked.
The helper image must be reprovisioned explicitly when upgrading this recipe;
do not delete it with unrelated image cleanup.

## Ownership and recovery

Deploy/Stop serialize through a shared canonical-controller lock and guarded
receipt updates. Candidate containers, networks and route fragments have exact
operation/project/MR/generation ownership. A candidate becomes healthy before
its HTTPS route changes. Failed nginx validation, reload or receipt writes
restore the previous route. Stop retains an owned HTTP 410 / HTTPS handshake-rejection tombstone so the
stopped host cannot fall through to a platform service, even without a usable
candidate certificate. Cleanup removes only the owned generation; stale
jobs cannot replace or stop a newer deployment.

A held lock after abrupt host/process loss requires operator inspection of its
owner and exact helper container before targeted recovery. Do not delete a lock,
receipt or route merely because a retry failed. Pending cutovers and retired
resources remain recorded for reconciliation. Never use global Docker prune or
restart the primary platform as cleanup.

Configuration stays separate from Harvest/Seed. Environment installation does
not select the primary development platform or promote the running Production
Wizard. Production uses the separate [operator promotion workflow](../wizard-production/README.md).

## Certificates without proxy downtime

Use an operator-provisioned ACME webroot shared at /ssl/acme-http01. The supplied
HTTP templates allow only /.well-known/acme-challenge/ before normal HTTPS
redirects. A default HTTP challenge server handles new candidate hosts before
their optional HTTPS route is installed. Do not stop the shared proxy for renewal.

For each certificate lineage, configure Certbot webroot authentication and a
deploy hook that atomically copies the full chain and private key into the
configured /ssl/live/<lineage>/ paths, validates nginx and gracefully reloads it.
Keep private keys private. Remove obsolete standalone stop/start renewal hooks
only after backing them up and validating the webroot renewal with a dry run.
Issuance and renewal remain operator tasks, not CI deployment privileges.

The isolated manifest covers environment API/workflow, deterministic recipes,
guarded GitLab upgrades, helper ownership/recovery and proxy preservation.
Also verify real GitLab manual-job execution, HTTPS/browser behavior and
preservation of Production on a disposable platform. Fixture success alone
does not prove those integration gates.

## One source-primary repository

An explicitly adopted source-primary Wizard project keeps its application source,
ordinary reviews and native build/environment jobs in one repository. It selects
`.gitlab/primary.yml`; it does not require a second application repository or
instance-specific committed marker files. The server-owned adoption receipt
binds the exact project ID, namespace, default branch and SHA-256 manifest of the
approved generic CI and build scripts. Jobs independently verify those files at
their actual pipeline commit. Editing the CI producers requires another reviewed
adoption; application changes follow the normal merge-request workflow.

The generic job launcher is `source-primary.sh`, installed in the application as
`.gitlab/delivery/environment.sh`. It accepts `deploy review`, `stop review`,
`deploy beta` or `stop beta`. Configure the following project CI variables with
the ordinary environment scope `*`, raw values, and no masking or protection:

| Variable | Operator-supplied value |
| --- | --- |
| `SYSTEM_WIZARD_ENVIRONMENT_IMAGE` | Exact preprovisioned clean System helper image ID, `sha256:…` |
| `SYSTEM_WIZARD_ENVIRONMENT_OPERATION` | New server-owned 48-character hexadecimal reservation identity |
| `WIZARD_REVIEW_HOST` | Exact configured Review HTTPS host, or empty when disabled |
| `WIZARD_BETA_HOST` | Exact configured Beta HTTPS host, or empty when disabled |

`WIZARD_DELIVERY_ENABLED=true` opts this instance into its native image build and
environment jobs. These configuration values are not credentials. They must be
available to same-project merge-request jobs; the canonical helper still rejects
jobs from other projects, forks, superseded reservations or unverified pipelines.
Production remains a separate deliberate promotion.

Before adopting an existing managed project, stop both optional environments and
use the existing owned stopped-route cleanup. Inspect its plan and confirm that
both old route fragments and their owned resources are absent. Adoption refuses
active, pending or retired generations. Keep the complete old deployment snapshot
in immutable history, and carry its generation floors into the new reservation.
Do not reset floors or rewrite old project tombstones as new project records.
An unexpected remaining route is rejected by the new helper.

The authenticated environment dialog continues to validate DNS and certificates
and update settings through an explicit preview. For a source-primary project it
updates only the four owned CI variables, without a source commit, new pipeline
or Production restart. Exact prior values and variable metadata are checked under
the existing lock. Interrupted partial updates retain the same operation; status
inspects them without writes, and explicit confirmation reconciles only known old
or target values. Unexpected variable changes require operator reconciliation.
The existing single Review lease, generation guards, bounded helper cleanup,
rollback and stopped-host behavior apply unchanged.

chapters.title: 8.5 Wizard Production and rollback
chapters.markdown:
# Deliberate Wizard Production promotion and recovery

Production promotion is an explicit operator command in the canonical controller, not an automatically enabled GitLab job.
Review/Beta remain separate manually deployed candidate environments.

## Preconditions and exact plan

Use the reviewed matching controller source and retain the previous Wizard image
on the daemon. A private own-GitLab pipeline must have successful required
`build:wizard` and `test:wizard` jobs with matching source/pipeline/registry digest
artifacts. Modern evidence must include lint, Vitest, TypeScript/build, rendered
UI, Projects, SPA, real configuration ZIP and exact Cube validation. Inspect a
separate candidate before applying Production. Pre-pull that exact registry
digest through the authenticated operator/runner; the helper never accepts a
tag or pulls with a provisioning credential.

Write a mode-0600 proof JSON below the persistent configuration directory, e.g.
`/state/wizard-production-proof.json` inside the controller:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "projectId": 42,
  "projectPath": "example/wizard",
  "pipelineId": 100,
  "sourceCommit": "REPLACE_WITH_THE_EXACT_GITLAB_PIPELINE_SHA",
  "imageRef": "registry.example.test/example/wizard@sha256:REPLACE_WITH_THE_64_HEX_DIGEST",
  "productionHost": "bootstrapper.example.test"
}
```

The IDs are examples; use the actual reviewed pipeline and image. Obtain a
read-only plan, review its current/target image IDs, hashes and host, then copy
its exact `planHash` into the apply command:

```sh
docker exec system_bootstrapper_1 node /system/project-bootstrap/wizard-production/run.js plan /state/wizard-production-proof.json
docker exec system_bootstrapper_1 node /system/project-bootstrap/wizard-production/run.js apply /state/wizard-production-proof.json PLAN_HASH
```

Apply independently verifies the exact private GitLab project, successful
pipeline, required non-optional jobs and matching artifacts via a temporary
server-side API credential which is revoked. No credentials or configuration
contents are printed. The current config, route, canonical container identity,
image and plan hash must still agree. The original 1184-character Cube stays
unchanged; image overrides are appended as literal assignments after it.

For an explicitly adopted [source-primary repository](../wizard-source-primary/README.md),
the native `.gitlab/primary.yml` path is accepted only for the exact canonical
project ID/path/namespace binding, enabled merge gates and approved CI-file hashes.
Its pipeline must be a native default-branch push at the current head, with all
required source and delivery jobs successful. A non-green `deploy:github`
publisher alone does not block the private workflow; other required failures,
skipped checks, unrelated jobs or missing evidence are rejected.
An unrelated project with similarly named jobs or an API-created pipeline is
rejected. Existing legacy `.system-bootstrapper/ci.yml` verification is unchanged.

## Cutover and retained state

The command acquires the existing persistent Wizard environment mutex. Sync
Push/control and other environment jobs respect this mutex. It atomically saves
a private checkpoint under `/state/wizard-production/`, then creates a uniquely
labeled candidate bounded to 128 MiB/0.5 CPU on the current Wizard network.
Only after that candidate is healthy does it update the single `upstream wizard`
address and validate/reload the existing NGINX process. Other routes are
preserved byte-for-byte. The old canonical Wizard is still running at this point.

While the checked candidate serves Production, the helper pins `WIZARD_IMAGE`
in persistent configuration, recreates only the canonical Wizard with
`--no-deps --pull never`, verifies its exact image and health, and redirects the
same upstream to its actual address. It does not restart the proxy, GitLab,
controller or runners. The checkpoint retains the previous immutable image ID,
private configuration/template bytes and the completed active hashes. Owned
candidate resources are then removed by full ID after checking their label.

A failed candidate does not recreate the canonical Wizard. A route/reload failure
restores the old route. A later failure recreates the previous immutable image,
uses its actual resulting address and restores the old configuration. Keep the
previous image and private checkpoint until deliberate rollback has been tested.

## Public operator details during cutover

Normal startup publishes only the six public website fields from signed saved
configuration into the persistent `wizard-public/privacy-instance.json` file.
The controller writes that directory; the canonical Wizard mounts it read-only
and serves `/privacy-instance.json` without Sync authentication. Edit these
values through **General → Website**, then Push normally. They remain
part of the ordinary JSON/environment/ZIP configuration backup. The sample
operator name, address and email are examples until replaced; explicitly cleared
values remain empty. Optional privacy text, notice URL and access-log retention
have no invented defaults.

Before promotion, prepare the updated persistent layout and replace the
controller with the matching reviewed image. This step does not require
replacing the current Wizard first. The promotion plan inspects the controller's
existing configuration and public bind-volume metadata, verifies that they are
siblings on the same mounted filesystem, and checks that the public JSON matches
the saved configuration. An existing canonical public mount must be read-only.

The temporary candidate receives only the validated public host directory as a
read-only bind mount. It receives no private configuration, credentials or
Docker socket. A missing source directory fails rather than creating a new
Docker-managed volume on the root disk. The first transition also supports an
older canonical Wizard without this public mount; the updated controller is
the authority for its already-provisioned public directory. Canonical recreation
and rollback retain the normal Compose mount. Prepare storage through the host
preflight; never bypass the mounted-volume/UUID checks to create this directory.

## Deliberate rollback

```sh
docker exec system_bootstrapper_1 node /system/project-bootstrap/wizard-production/run.js rollback-plan
docker exec system_bootstrapper_1 node /system/project-bootstrap/wizard-production/run.js rollback PLAN_HASH
```

Rollback requires the completed checkpoint to still match the live image,
configuration and route. It uses the same healthy-candidate cutover and preserves
current settings while selecting the retained previous image. It does not claim
that the previous image was built by the new pipeline.

## Interrupted or conflicting recovery

A concurrent file edit is never overwritten. If safe automatic rollback cannot
complete, the healthy owned candidate, private checkpoint and shared mutex remain
for reconciliation; ordinary Push/restart stays blocked. Do not delete this
mutex blindly or remove the candidate currently serving the interface.

After the original helper process has ended, inspect the private checkpoint and
resolve any external config/template edit explicitly. Then preview and confirm
recovery:

```sh
docker exec system_bootstrapper_1 node /system/project-bootstrap/wizard-production/run.js recover-plan
docker exec system_bootstrapper_1 node /system/project-bootstrap/wizard-production/run.js recover PLAN_HASH
```

Recovery refuses a still-running original process or a changed lock owner. It
requires the expected exact file contents, restores the previous image/route,
cleans only operation-owned candidates and releases only its matching mutex.
The checkpoint and image are local persistent recovery state, not a substitute
for the separate configuration ZIP and Harvest seed.

## Validation scope

Offline regressions cover stale confirmation, bad GitLab proof, candidate health,
lost create response, route reload failure, canonical health failure with a
changed rollback IP, concurrent writes, retained mutex/reconciliation and
explicit rollback. The Ruby proof fixture rejects private-project, source,
optional-job, digest and modern check mismatches and verifies token revocation.
These are component checks. Verify a real successful pipeline, separate
candidate, Production promotion and rollback on your own infrastructure before
relying on the procedure for a service you need to keep available.

chapters.outcome: A reviewed plan switches the Wizard deliberately and preserves an inspectable rollback path.

chapters.markdown:
# Managed Wizard upgrade v1

This operator workflow upgrades the source and toolchain of an existing
private, managed Wizard project. It never registers another project or changes
the Production UI, proxy, image pin, runner credentials, or environment routes.

## Migration contract

1. Read the signed canonical project configuration and validate its ownership,
   source marker, original source manifest, managed build/environment files and
   exact current default-branch head. Require stopped Review and Beta leases.
2. Preview a deterministic migration branch in that project, the validated
   public source snapshot, modern recipe, immutable clean helper, and affected
   paths. Preserve unknown project files; reject edited managed source instead
   of silently discarding local development.
3. After explicit confirmation, checkpoint the old configuration privately on
   the volume. A skipped preparation commit removes only verified managed paths
   on the isolated branch; source, build and environment commits recreate them
   with their required per-file activation identity. Preserve their original
   verifiable ancestry. Create one migration MR before the final commit, whose
   normal MR pipeline runs the required modern build and browser checks.
4. Reconcile lost GitLab responses by inspecting the same branch and markers;
   never blindly repeat an uncertain commit or MR request. Keep main and the
   canonical receipt unchanged during review.
5. After a reviewed fast-forward retaining all four commits, verify the current main
   files and exact successful pipeline artifacts, then atomically adopt the new
   receipt. Preserve previous workflow metadata, stopped generations and
   tombstones. A second adoption is a verified no-op.
6. Exercise the normal canonical Review, stop, main/Beta, stop and guarded
   Production promotion/rollback workflows separately. Verify their actual
   pipeline and runtime results; component tests do not substitute for them.

The matching modern controller/helper must be built and reviewed first. Do not
reuse an old helper image: it cannot validate the modern build recipe.

## Operator procedure

Run the reviewed code in the canonical controller with Node 24. Prepare its
validated `project-bootstrap/wizard-source/snapshot.json` matching the reviewed
System gitlink. Store an expiring GitLab API credential privately on the volume,
mode 0600, as `{ "baseUrl": "https://gitlab.example/api/v4", "token": "..." }`.
The API token is read from this file only, never a command argument, log, CI
variable, receipt, or checkpoint. Revoke it after the operation. It must belong
to the platform's own GitLab; TLS verification remains enabled.

Create a mode-0600 options file containing `credentialFile` and the exact
immutable `helperImage` (`sha256:...`) for the reviewed clean controller image.
Optional `config`, `mainConfig` and `directory` paths default to
`/state/.projects.env/.wizard.env`, `/state/.docker.env` and `/state/wizard-upgrades`.
The main configuration's own GitLab host and registry
are enforced. It is read and hash-checked, never rewritten by this workflow.
Before staging any write, a bounded networkless container verifies that the
selected helper image contains the exact reviewed environment/build dependency
files. It receives no Docker socket, state, certificates or credentials. The
operator must also set the canonical controller's
`SYSTEM_WIZARD_ENVIRONMENT_IMAGE` to that same image when rolling out the reviewed
controller. Keep the pre-pulled helper on the shared runner daemon.

```sh
node project-bootstrap/wizard-upgrade/run.js plan /state/upgrade-options.json
# Review source revision, project identity, branch, current head and path diff.
# Reserve a bounded CI slot before stage: its last commit starts CI.
node project-bootstrap/wizard-upgrade/run.js stage /state/upgrade-options.json PLAN_HASH
```

Inspect the returned existing-project MR and required `build:wizard` and
`test:wizard` jobs. The operator must review and temporarily select the existing
project's `merge_method=ff` if needed; this helper never changes project policy.
Merge only after review and success, **by fast-forward without squash or
rebase**, retaining all four checkpointed commits. Main must still equal the
previewed head immediately before that merge and exactly the final environment
commit at adoption. Do not edit the managed files in between. Identical file
contents require this history to preserve their new `last_commit_id` proof.
Restore the previous merge policy after adoption if desired. The old receipt
remains active until adoption.

```sh
node project-bootstrap/wizard-upgrade/run.js adoption-plan /state/upgrade-options.json
node project-bootstrap/wizard-upgrade/run.js adopt /state/upgrade-options.json ADOPTION_HASH
```

Adoption requires the exact staged MR pipeline to be green, both checks to be
required, matching modern evidence and registry digest, the MR to be merged,
and every staged source/managed file at current main to match its verified
commit. It records the original source revision, import/build/environment
receipts and stopped leases in `wizardWorkflow.upgradeHistory` and preserves
unrelated registration fields and configuration bytes. Its private checkpoint
also retains the original signed project configuration on the volume.

Create a normal small follow-up MR in the **same** project to verify manual
Review deploy/stop with the new helper. Merge it, verify manual Beta deploy/stop,
then use the separate `wizard-production/run.js` plan/apply/rollback procedure
with that canonical project's verified digest. No Production promotion occurs
as part of migration or adoption.

If a request loses its response, rerun `stage` with the original plan hash. It
adopts only an exact already-created commit/MR. An intent with no observable
result requires administrator inspection; it deliberately refuses another
blind POST. Never delete checkpoints or force-push to bypass this guard. A
concurrent config/main edit or active lease requires a fresh review, not an
automatic overwrite. Before adoption, abandon an unmerged migration by closing
its MR; main and the old receipt remain valid. After adoption, reverting source
alone is insufficient: use a separately reviewed inverse migration. Production
rollback uses its independent retained image/checkpoint.

## Build and environment recipes without reimporting source

Use the explicit `build-` actions when an already-modern managed project needs
the versioned cleanup correction, overview-compatible browser checks or refreshed
CA trust in its job images.
The ordinary source-upgrade actions still reject edited imported source. This
separate path accepts existing development, including added or removed source
files, and changes only the reserved build files, environment helper, managed
CI entrypoint and their two receipts. Without a `buildProfile` option it retains
the `node24-vite8-cleanup-v2` target and operation identity for existing
checkpoints. To prepare delivery of source with top-level Overview / Wizard
navigation, set `"buildProfile": "node24-vite8-overview-v3"` in the private
options file before previewing. This profile also verifies earlier modern source
that opens directly in the workspace, so recipe migration can precede the UI
change. Keep the same explicit target for stage, adoption and retries. Unknown
targets and accidental downgrades from the overview profile are rejected.

For the current public CA refresh, explicitly select
`"buildProfile": "node24-vite8-ca-v4"` and the accepted immutable helper before
previewing. This profile inherits the overview and cleanup checks and rebuilds
the affected build/browser images with the reviewed bundled trust data. Keep
the explicit profile through stage, adoption and retries; the omitted-option
historical target is not automatically changed. This guarded build-only migration
accepts modern profiles. `legacy-ca-v4` is available for new legacy-source
reservations; an existing legacy project follows the source/toolchain migration
to the supported modern profile.
Legacy projects still need the separately reviewed source/toolchain upgrade.
Historical recipe hashes and existing checkpoints remain verifiable.

```sh
node project-bootstrap/wizard-upgrade/run.js build-plan /state/upgrade-options.json
# Review scope=build-environment, exact head, managed paths and preservedTreeHash.
# Reserve a bounded CI slot before this final MR commit starts CI.
node project-bootstrap/wizard-upgrade/run.js build-stage /state/upgrade-options.json PLAN_HASH
# Review required build/browser jobs; fast-forward the MR without squash/rebase.
node project-bootstrap/wizard-upgrade/run.js build-adoption-plan /state/upgrade-options.json
node project-bootstrap/wizard-upgrade/run.js build-adopt /state/upgrade-options.json ADOPTION_HASH
```

The private checkpoint and migration operation are distinct from a source
upgrade. The three retained commits are preparation, build and environment.
Preparation deletes only verified managed recipe files and replaces the build
marker temporarily; it never writes the source/import marker. Build and
environment recreate unchanged files so their exact activation-commit proofs
remain valid. The source import revision, manifest, import commit and source
marker retain their original identities. Every other repository file is guarded
by a deterministic fingerprint of bytes, Git mode and last-change commit, checked
on each staged commit and again before adoption. Unexpected additions, removals,
content, mode or history changes fail the same operation rather than being
reimported or overwritten.

The existing ownership, immutable-helper verification, environment mutex,
configuration/main compare-and-swap, uncertain-write checkpoints, fast-forward
ancestry and exact required pipeline/artifact checks apply. Review and Beta must
be fully stopped before planning; their generation floors, tombstones and other
settings are preserved exactly. Stage keeps the old canonical receipt active.
Adoption changes only its managed workflow receipts and appends upgrade history;
configuration bytes outside the receipt remain unchanged. It never promotes the
candidate or changes the Production image pin. If the config was adopted but the
checkpoint write was interrupted, a verified repeated adoption repairs that
checkpoint without rewriting the config. Do not replace `build-stage` with a
source reimport to bypass a conflicting plan.

chapters.title: 8.7 One source-primary repository
chapters.markdown:
# One source-primary Wizard repository

An existing Wizard source repository can also own its native build, browser tests,
Review/Beta jobs and production images. Development and delivery then use one
project; a separate application repository is not required. An optional GitHub
mirror continues to publish reviewed source through the repository's normal CI.

This is an explicit operator adoption, not an automatic source import. The default
managed registration and its legacy initialization/upgrade workflows remain
available for installations that use them. Once adopted, the Wizard identifies
the canonical project by its exact GitLab ID, namespace and path. Source import
and legacy recipe upgrades refuse this mode instead of overwriting development.

## Prepare the repository and retained state

1. Retain a private export of the old project, all required Git references, its
   source/build/environment receipts and deployment checkpoints. Export required
   job evidence and registry images separately: a project export is not a complete
   registry or CI-artifact backup. Do not merge private deployment history into
   the public source branch to retain it.
2. Stop active Review/Beta environments and reconcile pending or retired leases.
   Use the existing stopped-environment cleanup helper before reassignment so
   old route fragments are removed by their verified owner. The adoption archive
   retains old tombstones unchanged; new slots retain their generation floors.
3. Review the source project's `.gitlab/primary.yml`. It must retain its source
   checks and intended publishing role, and provide required `build:wizard` and
   `test:wizard` jobs using the reviewed generic build recipe. Configure delivery
   explicitly with `WIZARD_DELIVERY_ENABLED=true` and the required runner access.
   Merge through normal reviews with successful-pipeline and discussion gates
   enabled. Do not skip or disable those gates.
4. Verify a native default-branch **push** pipeline for the exact resulting commit.
   Both delivery jobs must be required and successful. Their `build-evidence.json`
   and `wizard-evidence.json` must agree on the commit, pipeline ID and immutable
   image reference. The checks include Vitest, lint, TypeScript, production build,
   rendered UI, navigation, configuration ZIP and exact Cube signature.
   Required `build:source` and `test:browser` jobs must also succeed. A pending,
   running, failed or canceled `deploy:github` publisher alone does not block
   private delivery; its actual publishing status remains visible. Every other
   non-optional job must succeed. No required native check can be skipped or
   ignored, and normal merge gates remain enabled.
5. Build and review a matching controller/helper supporting source-primary mode.
   Retain the previous Wizard image on the daemon. Prepare the private environment
   variables described in the [environment guide](../wizard-environments/README.md).

## Preview and adopt

Create a private input JSON with these fields, using values from your own project
and verified pipeline:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "projectId": 42,
  "projectPath": "example/system-wizard",
  "namespaceId": 7,
  "defaultBranch": "master",
  "pipelineId": 100,
  "sourceCommit": "REPLACE_WITH_THE_EXACT_40_HEX_COMMIT",
  "imageRef": "registry.example.test/example/system-wizard@sha256:REPLACE_WITH_THE_64_HEX_DIGEST",
  "helperImage": "sha256:REPLACE_WITH_THE_REVIEWED_64_HEX_SYSTEM_IMAGE_ID",
  "ciFiles": [
    {"path": ".gitlab/primary.yml", "sha256": "REPLACE_WITH_64_HEX_SHA256_OF_EXACT_COMMITTED_BYTES"}
  ]
}
```

`ciFiles` is a complete approved CI manifest, not just the one illustrative row.
Include the native CI definition, its delivery/environment launcher, the generic
`.system-bootstrapper/build-v1/` recipe files and referenced `.gitlab/` scripts.
Compute each SHA-256 from the exact bytes at `sourceCommit`. The helper checks
those files through GitLab and independently validates the reserved generic
build recipe. Future changes to this manifest require another reviewed binding
operation; ordinary application changes can use the existing binding unchanged.

Store the input and an expiring GitLab API credential file mode `0600` beneath
the persistent configuration directory. The credential JSON contains `baseUrl`
and `token`; its TLS origin must match the configured own GitLab host. Credentials
and configuration contents are never printed. Revoke the operator credential
after use.

```sh
docker exec system_bootstrapper_1 node /system/project-bootstrap/wizard-source-primary/run.js plan /state/adoption-input.json /state/adoption-credential.json
docker exec system_bootstrapper_1 node /system/project-bootstrap/wizard-source-primary/run.js apply /state/adoption-input.json /state/adoption-credential.json PLAN_HASH
```

Review the exact plan hash, old/new project IDs, previous production image, new
pipeline/image and configuration hashes. Apply rechecks GitLab, acquires the
existing environment mutex, saves the complete old configuration/receipt privately
under `/state/wizard-source-primary/` and atomically changes only the project
binding. A stale confirmation or concurrent edit fails without overwriting it.
Repeating the same completed adoption is a verified no-op.

Adoption does not change the running production container or image pin. The one
exact previous image is recorded as an explicit recovery alias while the old
project still exists. A different digest or unrelated project is not accepted.
The Build status action reads native pipeline evidence without creating pipelines
or importing source. A pending or failed current default-branch pipeline is shown
as unverified rather than presenting an older build as current.

## Refresh an existing source-primary build recipe

A controller update preserves the existing build reservation. For an already
adopted modern Wizard, select `"buildProfile": "node24-vite8-ca-v4"` explicitly
in a new adoption input to upgrade that reservation. The accepted starting
profiles are `node24-vite8`, its cleanup-v2 and overview-v3 profiles, and CA-v4
itself. Legacy recipes and initial adoption cannot select this upgrade. Omitting
`buildProfile` retains the exact existing recipe and historical input hashes.

First open a normal merge request in the canonical Wizard source project. Use
the reviewed controller's `wizard-build/recipe.js` `generate(cube,
'node24-vite8-ca-v4')` result to install every returned `files` entry, including
the public CA bundle and refresh script. Preserve application source and update
the existing `.gitlab/primary.yml` rather than replacing it with the managed
recipe's separate CI document. Refresh the source and delivery job parents,
install the committed public bundle before network operations, and set
`NODE_OPTIONS=--use-openssl-ca` for Node jobs. Retain required source, browser and
delivery checks, the public mirror and environment jobs. Rebuild and test both
the delivery image and browser/job images; an old successful pipeline is not
evidence for the new trust inputs.

After review, merge and verify the exact default-branch push pipeline. Prepare
the new complete `ciFiles` manifest from that commit, its immutable image digest,
pipeline identity and matching reviewed helper. Stop and reconcile Review/Beta
and use the same `plan`/`apply` commands above. The plan includes the old and new
build recipe hashes. Apply independently verifies every approved CI hash and all
generic recipe bytes, retains the previous configuration and receipt in a new
private archive, and preserves canonical identity and environment generation
floors. A changed or missing CA file, unrelated recipe or required CI failure
refuses the binding. Production image promotion remains the separate step below.

## Promote and remove the duplicate

Pre-pull the exact new image through scoped registry authentication and use the
existing [production plan/apply workflow](../wizard-production/README.md). Its
source-primary verifier requires the canonical binding, approved CI manifest,
exact current default-branch push pipeline, required jobs and matching artifacts.
Production remains an operator promotion; a source merge alone does not switch it.

Verify the actual public UI, Review/Beta deploy/stop behavior, configuration Fetch,
native build status and cold image recovery from the adopted project. Preserve
the previous image and rollback checkpoint. Refresh recovery instructions and the
configuration backup so a new host uses the new project and registry pin.

Only then delete the duplicate project after confirming no live dependency remains.
Deleting it removes its registry endpoint; a historical rollback image from that
project must remain in a deliberate local/offline archive. The exact recovery alias
does not recreate a deleted registry or make old backups independent of it.
